title: Extra path after a PHP script is written into the page unescaped
summary: A PHP page accepts extra path after its own name (page.php/anything) and writes it back into the HTML without encoding it, usually through $_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] in a form action or a link. A link with markup in that extra path puts the markup on the page: a meta refresh that sends the visitor to any site, a fake sign in form, or script where the content security policy allows it.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist.  The marker only ever goes in the probe, so a page that shows it unescaped wrote the request's own path into its markup.
confirm.differential: status_in(200) and body_contains('"><gcrpi7q>') and 'html' in header('content-type')

reproduce: curl -sk "https://host/index.php/x%22%3E%3Cb%3Etest%3C/b%3E" and look for the literal text ">test in the page, unescaped (not "><b>). Try the other script names the rule lists, and any other PHP page on the site. In a browser, a meta refresh in the same place sends the visitor to another site.
remediate: Encode the value before writing it into HTML: htmlspecialchars($_SERVER['PHP_SELF'], ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'). Better, do not use PHP_SELF or REQUEST_URI in markup at all: leave a form's action empty to post back to the same page, or write the script's fixed path. Turning off AcceptPathInfo in Apache also stops the extra path from reaching the script.
